name: s1-metabolic-partnership
title: S1 — Metabolic partnership: can an archaeal-bacterial pair gain fitness from exchange?
concept: Syntrophy and mutualism made operational as exchange fluxes, partner-dependent growth, invasion fitness, and environmental contingencies. Curated candidate genomes -> gap-audited genome-scale models (GEMs) -> two-member community FBA / dynamic FBA, with separate positive and negative controls, under alternative redox and substrate regimes.
question: Can plausible archaeal-bacterial pairs gain fitness from metabolite exchange, and under which redox and substrate regimes? Does the predicted mutualism survive mass-balance and electron-donor/acceptor feasibility audits and alternative reconstructions?
hypothesis: Under at least one field-consistent redox/substrate regime, a reconstructed archaeal-host / bacterial-partner pair achieves partner-dependent growth (each grows better together than alone) on mass-balanced exchange fluxes, while a no-exchange / parasitic control does not.
claim: An archaeal-bacterial association can become mutually beneficial under restricted redox and substrate regimes — a connected cross-feeding community develops functional redundancy that an isolated (no-exchange) control does not, on mass-balanced exchange — but the benefit is not necessarily stable or obligate and disappears outside the feasible regime.

behavior_tests.name: community-redundancy-develops
behavior_tests.description: The connected community develops functional redundancy — a majority of protometabolic capabilities held by >= 2 compartments (robust to a single-compartment loss). This only rises above the ~0.46 seeded floor when cross-feeding fills in capabilities, so the >0.5 threshold discriminates the connected community from the isolated (no-exchange) control: the partner dependence IS the gap between the two arms.

provenance.note: Calibrated at p_diacid=1e-8, p_monoacid=1e-7, k_wash=0.01, 250 steps (og-07 nominal): the connected arm (coupling=shared) settles to 0.536 (PASS) while the isolated control (coupling=private, the `isolated-control` variant) settles to 0.464 (FAIL) — a partner-dependent advantage of connected/isolated = 1.15. A majority of capabilities are redundantly covered only with cross-feeding.

behavior_tests.name: exchange-mass-balanced
behavior_tests.description: Exchanged metabolites close an elemental carbon mass balance (no free lunch).

provenance.note: Exchange fluxes must conserve carbon; worst-case C residual stays ~0 (observed 5.6e-11).

findings.statement: Calibrated (p_diacid=1e-8, p_monoacid=1e-7, k_wash=0.01, 250 steps): the connected cross-feeding community settles to metacommunity_robustness 0.536 (> 0.5, PASS) while the isolated control (coupling=private) settles to 0.464 (< 0.5, FAIL) — a partner-dependent advantage of 1.15 (connected/isolated). Carbon mass balance holds (worst-case residual 5.6e-11). Establishes a mechanistically plausible route (connected community) and a well-characterized failure route (isolated control) at first fidelity. Computed via a direct in-process composite run; the tracked workbench run awaits the evaluator reaching the genesis venv.

provenance.note: In-process run of metabolite_exchange_community (lineages fixer:4,reducer:4, reaction_universe, p_diacid 1e-8, p_monoacid 1e-7, k_wash 0.01, 250 steps). Connected (coupling=shared) settles to metacommunity_robustness 0.536 (>0.5); isolated control (coupling=private) 0.464. Robustness develops over ~200 steps — a 60-step run is too short (0.43) and under-reads the connected advantage.

findings.statement: The isolated no-exchange control (coupling=private) settles to metacommunity_robustness 0.464 (< 0.5) — without reciprocal exchange the community does not develop functional redundancy. The partner-dependent advantage (connected 0.536 vs isolated 0.464) is the discriminating signal.

provenance.note: Same composite, isolated counterfactual (coupling=private), 250 steps: metacommunity_robustness 0.464.

literature_anchors.expectation: Syntrophic archaeal-bacterial growth is observed in Prometheoarchaeum syntrophicum.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: First-fidelity arm. settled_metacommunity_robustness (community functional redundancy) is the partner-dependence gate; C_residual_max gives carbon mass balance. The next-fidelity arm — two gap-audited archaeal/alphaproteobacterial GEMs under community FBA — is blocked on COBRApy (not installed) + genome reconstruction (GTDB/NCBI data not yet ingested).
